prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE isolated living Glebionis coronaria edible crown daisy / shungiku / 茼蒿 plant, medium narrow deeply lobed leaf type, as image-to-3D reference for a Jiangnan miniature farm. Image 1 is STYLE ONLY, approved Chinese gongbi light-colour painting: fresh muted sage/jade greens, layered watercolor pigment mottling, deliberate fine moss-green contours and structural midrib lines. Do not copy bok choy anatomy, white thick stems or inflated leaves. Other images are botanical shape references only. A convincing volumetric plant with ROUND slender green stems and THIN softly cupped leaves facing varied directions; camera elevated 35 degrees downward in three-quarter view, clear front/back overlap and depth, not a flat herbarium fan. Plain uniform neutral light-gray background. Full silhouette with generous margins. Matte diffuse even light; no cast shadow, no pots, soil, loose balls, base disk, roots, flowers, text or other objects. All stems connected to ONE short basal planting anchor, all leaves visibly above anchor. Preserve clear delicate ink-and-wash brushwork, not glossy photorealism or neon green. Intermediate vegetative stage: one compact short upright green main stem carrying SIX true leaves distributed alternately in a three-dimensional spiral at different heights, plus one small central growing tip. Each true leaf is elongated with deep rounded-to-triangular lobes along both sides of a continuous midrib blade (pinnatifid, NOT many disconnected leaflets). About 3-4 pairs of lobes per larger leaf and a rounded terminal lobe; narrow upper leaves. Lower leaves spread laterally but remain above the basal planting anchor. Loose open small plant with visible stem structure and natural leaf cupping, no dense mature crown, no branching flower stalk.
revision_prompt: Edit this crown daisy reference, keep its species, exact lobed leaf anatomy, fine ink contour/vein marks and watercolor mottled sage-green texture. Transform only the plant's spatial pose and viewpoint into an unmistakably THREE-DIMENSIONAL living plant. View DOWN from 45 degrees above at a three-quarter angle. Leaves spiral around the round stem in ALL directions: foreground leaves foreshortened toward viewer, two side leaves almost edge-on, several back leaves receding with overlap. Do NOT show all leaf faces frontally. Stems cylindrical, leaf surfaces thin gently cupped and bent, visible depth about equal to width. Roots hidden: show one short planting anchor below ALL leaf tips, no leaves pointing below the root base. No soil, pot, pedestal, loose particles, flowers, text or cast shadow. Uniform light-gray background. Preserve the handmade painted texture while using clear diffuse 3D shading; no glossy rubber surfaces. Shorten main stem internodes by 35 percent for a compact juvenile, keep six main leaves and the small central growing tip, remove excessive small side leaves; no branches.
